passages.text: At that time the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and in it they found the passage stating that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, because they had not met the Israelites with food and water, but had hired Balaam to call down a curse against them (although our God had turned the curse into a blessing).
passages.sermon:
The people gathered together on that day.
Someone read the Book of Moses aloud to everyone.
The people listened to the words of the book.
They found a command written in the book.
The command said that no Ammonite may enter the assembly of God.
The command also said that no Moabite may enter the assembly of God.
This rule would last forever.
The Ammonites and Moabites did not welcome the Israelites with bread and water.
Instead, the Ammonites and Moabites hired Balaam.
They wanted Balaam to curse the Israelites.
But God changed the curse into a blessing.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נִקְרָ֛א בְּסֵ֥פֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וְנִמְצָא֙ כָּת֣וּב בּ֔וֹ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־ יָב֨וֹא עַמֹּנִ֧י וּמֹאָבִ֛י בִּקְהַ֥ל הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃ כִּ֣י לֹ֧א קִדְּמ֛וּ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּלֶּ֣חֶם וּבַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֨ר עָלָ֤יו אֶת־ בִּלְעָם֙ לְקַֽלְל֔וֹ וַיַּהֲפֹ֧ךְ אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ הַקְּלָלָ֖ה לִבְרָכָֽה׃

passages.text: As soon as the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all of foreign descent.
passages.sermon:
The people heard the law of God.
They listened to the words of the Torah.
They understood what God commanded.
They acted immediately.
They separated everyone of foreign descent from Israel.
They made sure only Israelites remained among them.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י כְּשָׁמְעָ֣ם אֶת־ הַתּוֹרָ֑ה וַיַּבְדִּ֥ילוּ כָל־ עֵ֖רֶב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, a relative of Tobiah, had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God and had prepared for Tobiah a large room where they had previously stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the temple articles, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the contributions for the priests.
passages.sermon:
Eliashib was a priest.
Eliashib was related to Tobiah.
People put Eliashib in charge of the storerooms in the house of our God.
Eliashib prepared a large room for Tobiah.
People had used this room before to store important items.
They stored the grain offerings in this room.
They stored the frankincense in this room.
They stored the temple articles in this room.
They stored the tithes of grain in this room.
They stored the tithes of new wine in this room.
They stored the tithes of oil in this room.
These tithes were for the Levites.
These tithes were for the singers.
These tithes were for the gatekeepers.
They also stored the contributions for the priests in this room.
passages.original: וְלִפְנֵ֣י מִזֶּ֔ה אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נָת֖וּן בְּלִשְׁכַּ֣ת בֵּית־ אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ קָר֖וֹב לְטוֹבִיָּֽה׃ וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֜וֹ לִשְׁכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֗ה וְשָׁ֣ם הָי֪וּ לְפָנִ֟ים נֹ֠תְנִים אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֨ה הַלְּבוֹנָ֜ה וְהַכֵּלִ֗ים וּמַעְשַׂ֤ר הַדָּגָן֙ הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֔ר מִצְוַת֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִ֑ים וּתְרוּמַ֖ת הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

passages.text: While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem, because I had returned to Artaxerxes king of Babylon in the thirty-second year of his reign. Some time later I obtained leave from the king to return to Jerusalem. Then I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done on behalf of Tobiah by providing him a room in the courts of the house of God.
passages.sermon:
I was not in Jerusalem during all these events.
I had gone to Artaxerxes, king of Babylon.
This happened in the thirty-second year of his reign.
After some time, I asked the king for permission to leave.
The king allowed me to return to Jerusalem.
When I arrived in Jerusalem, I learned about a wrong action.
Eliashib had done something evil for Tobiah.
Eliashib gave Tobiah a room in the courts of the house of God.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ זֶ֕ה לֹ֥א הָיִ֖יתִי בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֡י בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֜יִם לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֤סְתְּא מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ בָּ֣אתִי אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְקֵ֥ץ יָמִ֖ים נִשְׁאַ֥לְתִּי מִן־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וָאָב֖וֹא לִֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וָאָבִ֣ינָה בָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ לְט֣וֹבִיָּ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לוֹ֙ נִשְׁכָּ֔ה בְּחַצְרֵ֖י בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: And I was greatly displeased and threw all of Tobiah’s household goods out of the room.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Jerusalem.
He returned to Jerusalem after being away.
He saw that Eliashib the priest had given Tobiah a room in the temple.
Nehemiah became very displeased.
He threw all of Tobiah’s household goods out of the room.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥רַֽע לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד וָֽאַשְׁלִ֜יכָה אֶֽת־ כָּל־ כְּלֵ֧י בֵית־ טוֹבִיָּ֛ה הַח֖וּץ מִן־ הַלִּשְׁכָּֽה׃

passages.text: Then I ordered that the rooms be purified, and I had the articles of the house of God restored to them, along with the grain offerings and frankincense.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Jerusalem.
He saw that Eliashib had given Tobiah a room in the temple courts.
Nehemiah became very upset.
He ordered the rooms to be purified.
The people cleansed the rooms.
Nehemiah returned the articles of the house of God to the rooms.
He also put the grain offerings and frankincense back in their place.
passages.original: וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה וַֽיְטַהֲר֖וּ הַלְּשָׁכ֑וֹת וָאָשִׁ֣יבָה שָּׁ֗ם כְּלֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֖ה וְהַלְּבוֹנָֽה׃פ

passages.text: I also learned that because the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, all the Levites and singers responsible for performing the service had gone back to their own fields.
passages.sermon:
The Levites served in the house of God.
The singers also served in the house of God.
They performed the work required for worship.
I learned something important.
The people did not give the Levites their portions.
The Levites did not receive what they needed.
The singers also did not receive their portions.
Because of this, the Levites left their service.
The singers also left their service.
Each Levite returned to his own field.
Each singer returned to his own field.
They went back to work in their own land.
passages.original: וָאֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּֽי־ מְנָי֥וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לֹ֣א נִתָּ֑נָה וַיִּבְרְח֧וּ אִישׁ־ לְשָׂדֵ֛הוּ הַלְוִיִּ֥ם וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים עֹשֵׂ֥י הַמְּלָאכָֽה׃

passages.text: So I rebuked the officials and asked, “Why has the house of God been neglected?” Then I gathered the Levites and singers together and stationed them at their posts, and all Judah brought a tenth of the grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Jerusalem.
He saw that the house of God was being neglected.
He rebuked the officials.
He asked them, "Why has the house of God been neglected?"
He gathered the Levites and the singers.
He stationed the Levites and singers at their posts.
All the people of Judah brought a tenth of their grain.
They also brought a tenth of their new wine.
They also brought a tenth of their oil.
They put these offerings into the storerooms.
passages.original: וָאָרִ֙יבָה֙ אֶת־ הַסְּגָנִ֔ים וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה מַדּ֖וּעַ נֶעֱזַ֣ב בֵּית־ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וָֽאֶ֨קְבְּצֵ֔ם וָֽאַעֲמִדֵ֖ם עַל־ עָמְדָֽם׃ וְכָל־ יְהוּדָ֗ה הֵבִ֜יאוּ מַעְשַׂ֧ר הַדָּגָ֛ן וְהַתִּיר֥וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֖ר לָאוֹצָרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I appointed as treasurers over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, with Hanan son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, to assist them, because they were considered trustworthy. They were responsible for distributing the supplies to their fellow Levites.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah appointed men to oversee the storerooms in the temple.
He chose Shelemiah, who was a priest.
He chose Zadok, who was a scribe.
He chose Pedaiah, who was from the Levites.
He also appointed Hanan to help them.
Hanan was the son of Zaccur.
Zaccur was the son of Mattaniah.
Nehemiah chose these men because people considered them trustworthy.
Their job was to distribute the supplies to the other Levites.
passages.original: וָאוֹצְרָ֣ה עַל־ א֠וֹצָרוֹת שֶׁלֶמְיָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְצָד֣וֹק הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וּפְדָיָה֙ מִן־ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְעַל־ יָדָ֔ם חָנָ֥ן בֶּן־ זַכּ֖וּר בֶּן־ מַתַּנְיָ֑ה כִּ֤י נֶאֱמָנִים֙ נֶחְשָׁ֔בוּ וַעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לַחֲלֹ֥ק לַאֲחֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Remember me for this, O my God, and do not blot out my deeds of loving devotion for the house of my God and for its services.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a leader in Jerusalem.
He prayed to God.
He said, "My God, remember me for this."
He asked God not to erase his deeds of loving devotion.
He did these deeds for the house of his God.
He also served in its duties.
passages.original: זָכְרָה־ לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י עַל־ זֹ֑את וְאַל־ תֶּ֣מַח חֲסָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהַ֖י וּבְמִשְׁמָרָֽיו׃

passages.text: In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, and figs. All kinds of goods were being brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I warned them against selling food on that day.
passages.sermon:
In those days, I saw people in Judah.
They were treading winepresses on the Sabbath.
They were bringing in grain.
They were loading grain on donkeys.
They were also bringing wine, grapes, and figs.
They brought all kinds of goods into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
I warned them on the day they sold food.
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֡מָּה רָאִ֣יתִי בִֽיהוּדָ֣ה׀ דֹּֽרְכִֽים־ גִּתּ֣וֹת׀ בַּשַּׁבָּ֡ת וּמְבִיאִ֣ים הָעֲרֵמ֣וֹת וְֽעֹמְסִ֪ים עַל־ הַחֲמֹרִ֟ים וְאַף־ יַ֜יִן עֲנָבִ֤ים וּתְאֵנִים֙ וְכָל־ מַשָּׂ֔א וּמְבִיאִ֥ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וָאָעִ֕יד בְּי֖וֹם מִכְרָ֥ם צָֽיִד׃

passages.text: Additionally, men of Tyre who lived there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Men from Tyre lived in Jerusalem.
These men brought fish into the city.
They also brought all kinds of merchandise.
They sold these goods on the Sabbath day.
They sold them to the people of Judah.
They sold them in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְהַצֹּרִים֙ יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ מְבִיאִ֥ים דָּ֖אג וְכָל־ מֶ֑כֶר וּמֹכְרִ֧ים בַּשַּׁבָּ֛ת לִבְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Then I rebuked the nobles of Judah and asked, “What is this evil you are doing—profaning the Sabbath day?
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Judah.
Nehemiah saw the nobles of Judah breaking the Sabbath.
Nehemiah rebuked the nobles of Judah.
Nehemiah said to them, “What is this evil thing you are doing?
You are profaning the Sabbath day.”
passages.original: וָאָרִ֕יבָה אֵ֖ת חֹרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם מָֽה־ הַדָּבָ֨ר הָרָ֤ע הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים וּֽמְחַלְּלִ֖ים אֶת־ י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃

passages.text: Did not your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? And now you are rekindling His wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath!”
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah had forefathers who lived before them.
Their forefathers also broke the Sabbath.
Their forefathers did evil things.
God saw what their forefathers did.
God brought disaster on the people because of their forefathers’ actions.
God also brought disaster on the city because of their forefathers’ actions.
Now the people of Judah are doing the same evil things.
They are profaning the Sabbath.
They are making God angry again against Israel.
passages.original: הֲל֨וֹא כֹ֤ה עָשׂוּ֙ אֲבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וַיָּבֵ֨א אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ עָלֵ֗ינוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְעַ֖ל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְאַתֶּ֞ם מוֹסִיפִ֤ים חָרוֹן֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְחַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־ הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃פ

passages.text: When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates so that no load could enter on the Sabbath day.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Jerusalem.
He wanted the people to keep the Sabbath holy.
As evening came and shadows fell on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I gave an order.
I commanded that the gates be shut.
I said the gates must not be opened until after the Sabbath.
I placed some of my servants at the gates.
I did this so that no load could enter Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צָֽלֲלוּ֩ שַׁעֲרֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לִפְנֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת וָאֹֽמְרָה֙ וַיִּסָּגְר֣וּ הַדְּלָת֔וֹת וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יִפְתָּח֔וּם עַ֖ד אַחַ֣ר הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וּמִנְּעָרַ֗י הֶֽעֱמַ֙דְתִּי֙ עַל־ הַשְּׁעָרִ֔ים לֹא־ יָב֥וֹא מַשָּׂ֖א בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃

passages.text: Once or twice, the merchants and those who sell all kinds of goods camped outside Jerusalem, but I warned them, “Why are you camping in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.” From that time on, they did not return on the Sabbath.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Jerusalem.
Nehemiah saw merchants outside Jerusalem.
These merchants sold all kinds of goods.
They camped outside the city once or twice.
Nehemiah warned the merchants.
He said, “Why are you camping in front of the wall?”
He said, “If you do this again, I will lay hands on you.”
After Nehemiah’s warning, the merchants did not return on the Sabbath.
passages.original: וַיָּלִ֨ינוּ הָרֹכְלִ֜ים וּמֹכְרֵ֧י כָל־ מִמְכָּ֛ר מִח֥וּץ לִירוּשָׁלִָ֖ם פַּ֥עַם וּשְׁתָּֽיִם׃ וָאָעִ֣ידָה בָהֶ֗ם וָאֹמְרָ֤ה אֲלֵיהֶם֙ מַדּ֜וּעַ אַתֶּ֤ם לֵנִים֙ נֶ֣גֶד הַחוֹמָ֔ה אִם־ תִּשְׁנ֕וּ יָ֖ד אֶשְׁלַ֣ח בָּכֶ֑ם מִן־ הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא לֹא־ בָ֖אוּ בַּשַּׁבָּֽת׃ס

passages.text: Then I instructed the Levites to purify themselves and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this as well, O my God, and show me mercy according to Your abundant loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
I spoke to the Levites.
The Levites are the tribe chosen to serve God in the temple.
I told the Levites to purify themselves.
I told the Levites to guard the gates of Jerusalem.
Their purpose was to keep the Sabbath day holy.
I asked God to remember this good deed.
I asked God to show me mercy.
God has great loving devotion.
passages.original: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִֽהְי֤וּ מִֽטַּהֲרִים֙ וּבָאִים֙ שֹׁמְרִ֣ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֔ים לְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־ י֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת גַּם־ זֹאת֙ זָכְרָה־ לִּ֣י אֱלֹהַ֔י וְח֥וּסָה עָלַ֖י כְּרֹ֥ב חַסְדֶּֽךָ׃פ

passages.text: In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader of the Jews in Jerusalem.
He saw what the people were doing.
He saw that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod.
He saw that some Jewish men had married women from Ammon.
He saw that some Jewish men had married women from Moab.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם׀ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־ הַיְּהוּדִים֙ הֹשִׁ֗יבוּ נָשִׁים֙ אַשְׁדּוֹדִיּוֹת עַמּוֹנִיּוֹת מוֹאֲבִיּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or of the other peoples, but could not speak the language of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The children of these Jews had foreign mothers from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half of these children spoke the language of Ashdod.
Some spoke the languages of other peoples.
They could not speak the language of Judah.
Each child spoke the language of his own people.
passages.original: וּבְנֵיהֶ֗ם חֲצִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אַשְׁדּוֹדִ֔ית וְאֵינָ֥ם מַכִּירִ֖ים לְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוּדִ֑ית וְכִלְשׁ֖וֹן עַ֥ם וָעָֽם׃

passages.text: I rebuked them and called down curses on them. I beat some of these men and pulled out their hair. Then I made them take an oath before God and said, “You must not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves!
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader of the Jews in Jerusalem.
He saw that some Jews had married foreign women.
He became very angry with these men.
He rebuked them.
He called down curses on them.
He beat some of the men.
He pulled out their hair.
He made them take an oath before God.
He said, “You must not give your daughters to their sons in marriage.
You must not take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves.”
passages.original: וָאָרִ֤יב עִמָּם֙ וָאֲקַֽלְלֵ֔ם וָאַכֶּ֥ה מֵהֶ֛ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וָֽאֶמְרְטֵ֑ם וָאַשְׁבִּיעֵ֣ם בֵּֽאלֹהִ֗ים אִם־ תִּתְּנ֤וּ בְנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ לִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְאִם־ תִּשְׂאוּ֙ מִבְּנֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֖ם וְלָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Did not King Solomon of Israel sin in matters like this? There was not a king like him among many nations, and he was loved by his God, who made him king over all Israel—yet foreign women drew him into sin.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
God loved Solomon.
God made Solomon king over all Israel.
No other king among many nations was like Solomon.
Yet Solomon sinned in matters like this.
Foreign women led Solomon into sin.
passages.original: הֲל֣וֹא עַל־ אֵ֣לֶּה חָטָֽא־ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וּבַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָרַבִּים֩ לֹֽא־ הָיָ֨ה מֶ֜לֶךְ כָּמֹ֗הוּ וְאָה֤וּב לֵֽאלֹהָיו֙ הָיָ֔ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֣הוּ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גַּם־ אוֹת֣וֹ הֶחֱטִ֔יאוּ הַנָּשִׁ֖ים הַנָּכְרִיּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Must we now hear that you too are doing all this terrible evil and acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?”
passages.sermon:
You are doing a very great evil.
You are being unfaithful to our God.
You are marrying foreign women.
Must we now hear that you are doing these things too?
passages.original: וְלָכֶ֣ם הֲנִשְׁמַ֗ע לַעֲשֹׂת֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את לִמְעֹ֖ל בֵּֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְהֹשִׁ֖יב נָשִׁ֥ים נָכְרִיּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Even one of the sons of Jehoiada son of Eliashib the high priest had become a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I drove him away from me.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiada was the son of Eliashib.
Eliashib was the high priest.
One of Jehoiada’s sons married Sanballat’s daughter.
Sanballat was a Horonite.
I saw this marriage.
I drove Jehoiada’s son away from me.
passages.original: וּמִבְּנֵ֨י יוֹיָדָ֤ע בֶּן־ אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל חָתָ֖ן לְסַנְבַלַּ֣ט הַחֹרֹנִ֑י וָאַבְרִיחֵ֖הוּ מֵעָלָֽי׃

passages.text: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
passages.sermon:
God, you know all things.
Some people have defiled the priesthood.
They have broken the covenant of the priesthood.
They have also broken the covenant of the Levites.
God, remember these people.
passages.original: זָכְרָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם אֱלֹהָ֑י עַ֚ל גָּאֳלֵ֣י הַכְּהֻנָּ֔ה וּבְרִ֥ית הַכְּהֻנָּ֖ה וְהַלְוִיִּֽם׃

passages.text: Thus I purified the priests and Levites from everything foreign, and I assigned specific duties to each of the priests and Levites.
passages.sermon:
The priests and the Levites served God in the temple.
Some of them had become involved with foreign practices.
I purified the priests and the Levites from everything foreign.
I removed all foreign influences from them.
I gave each priest his own duty.
I gave each Levite his own duty.
Each person served in his own work.
passages.original: וְטִֽהַרְתִּ֖ים מִכָּל־ נֵכָ֑ר וָאַעֲמִ֧ידָה מִשְׁמָר֛וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ בִּמְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I also arranged for contributions of wood at the appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, with favor.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah led the people of Israel.
He arranged for offerings of wood.
He set specific times for these offerings.
He also arranged for the offering of firstfruits.
He asked God to remember him for good.
passages.original: וּלְקֻרְבַּ֧ן הָעֵצִ֛ים בְּעִתִּ֥ים מְזֻמָּנ֖וֹת וְלַבִּכּוּרִ֑ים זָכְרָה־ לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָֽה׃
